title: Chauncey Holland and Al Travis as band bookers
summary: Albert praises Chauncey Holland and Al Travis as salesmen who could book a band solidly, regretting that Travis was crooked.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: the glass floor. What about, was Chauncey Holland a good salesman? One of the best.
Any time a man can sell a band for five nights or six nights in a row and book them in two, three towns at the same time, he's got to be good. Same with Al Travis.
Well it's funny, they could have made honest money.

They sure they could have made a bunch of, all Al Travis would have had to do was continue the bookers from Florida back into New York and we possibly would have gone into all of the major, major spots because he knew how to sell it. That is really weird to me, you know, that a man could be such a successful salesman. And he's so crooked and so no good. And if he leaves the few bucks that he would have been doing, he would have been doing it. He would have built that up into a repeat there. That's going to be a guy for a while. Yeah, sure. Yeah, sure. Because he actually was getting us good prices.
